newsitem.title: UK: Gulf Canada says Clyde counterbid unlikely.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Canada says Clyde counterbid unlikely.

text.p: Gulf Canada Resources Ltd said on Tuesday it was unlikely its hostile 432 million stg offer for Clyde Petroleum Plc will be trumped by a rival bidder.
Gulf chief financial officer Greg Glick told journalists any potential rival bidders would not been able to detect value not already appreciated in Gulf's 105 pence per share offer.
"When other companies look at Clyde they are going to see the same thing as we did," Glick said during a press conference call.
Shares in Clyde were trading down 2-1/2 pence at 120-1/2 with many analysts saying they don't expect the company to be taken out at lower levels.
But Glick said the share price was driven well above Gulf's bid because of "arbitrage" and added he was confident the shares would come down shortly.
Gulf Canada was not disappointed that just 0.02 percent of Clyde's issued share capital had been tendered up until January 10. Glick said this kind of level was expected.

He lashed out at Clyde's growth potential, saying that its forecast production growth was among the worst in the oil exploration and production sector. "Their production growth rates second to last off all their peers," said Glick.
It also explained why Clyde was trading at such as low cash flow multiple, Glick said. "A lower multiple is justified because there is no growth," Glick said.
"We are not going to pay for exploration upside which is not there," he added.
Clyde earlier pointed to its low cash flow multiple compared with other firms to show that Gulf Resources' offer was too low.

Rather than Clyde growth prospects, Glick said Gulf Canada was interested in the British firm because of the location of its main assets: the North Sea and offshore Australia, which were politically stable regions with favourable tax regimes.
Gulf Resources launched its hostile offer in December.
